section_summary: This section covers Japanese fishing and Antarctic whaling under the Allied occupation, including proposed fishing-area expansions, whaling oversight, catch statistics, and plans for a 1948–49 expedition. It also records a proposed American–Japanese crab-canning venture near Soviet waters, requests about Bering Sea fishing, and concern over Japanese tuna imports. Several pages reproduce a Tokyo despatch and its enclosures in duplicate.

subfiles.title: Norwegian merchant-vessel depreciation allowances
subfiles.about: Reports Norwegian depreciation rates for ships and rules for writing off inflated purchase costs.
subfiles.summary: Lists annual depreciation rates by vessel type and explains limits on carrying allowances forward and writing off inflated asset costs.

subfiles.title: Conversation with United Press on Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Explains international limits on the current Japanese whaling expedition and the absence of authorization for another season.
subfiles.summary: Flory described catch and season limits and said a future expedition remained undecided.

subfiles.title: Transmitting “Hunting the Whale”
subfiles.from: Everett F. Drumright, American Embassy, London
subfiles.about: Forwards a newspaper article on declining whale stocks and criticism of Japanese whaling.
subfiles.summary: Flags the article’s misleading claim that Japanese whalers would lack foreign supervision.

subfiles.title: “Hunting the Whale”
subfiles.about: Argues that the Antarctic whale catch limit threatens stocks and criticizes Japanese whaling practices.
subfiles.summary: Describes the postwar whaling fleet, the 16,000 blue-whale-unit quota, disagreement over sustainability, and allegations that Japanese crews waste catches and lack adequate supervision.

subfiles.title: Reply to Norwegian aide-mémoire concerning Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Records a Norwegian Embassy visit about Japanese whaling, German trawlers, and the whaling protocol.
subfiles.summary: Lykke accepted assurances that Norway’s concerns would reach SCAP and raised separate concerns about trawling off northern Norway.

subfiles.title: Proposed American fishing operations off Soviet North Pacific coasts
subfiles.about: Discusses Hubert D. Long’s proposed American-flag crab-canning operation using Japanese capital and labor near Soviet waters.
subfiles.summary: Long sought guidance on high-seas fishing rights and protection against Soviet interference. Officials distinguished legal fishing rights from decisions about diplomatic protection and ruled out a promise of naval assistance.

subfiles.title: File note on replying to Hubert D. Long
subfiles.about: Explains why no written reply to Long’s fishing inquiry would be sent.
subfiles.summary: Long’s letter to the Soviet Embassy misstated State Department involvement.

subfiles.title: Proposal for American-flag crab canneries
subfiles.about: Requests clear guidance on fishing near Soviet waters and possible American protection.
subfiles.summary: Long outlines a venture with a Japanese firm using American floating canneries and Japanese crews and capital, then asks about high-seas fishing rights and naval protection.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Soviet Embassy about crab fishing
subfiles.about: Asks the Soviet government’s attitude toward American crab fishing outside and potentially inside its territorial waters.
subfiles.summary: Long proposes floating canneries near the Bering Sea, Sea of Okhotsk, and Sakhalin, and inaccurately states that the State Department referred him to the Soviet Embassy.

subfiles.title: Request for 1947 Japanese whaling statistics
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP reports on Japan’s 1947 whale catch for the International Bureau of Whaling Statistics.
subfiles.summary: Paulsen appreciated the 1946 reports and requested corresponding 1947 figures.

subfiles.title: Reply on transmission of Japanese whaling reports
subfiles.about: Says SCAP will be asked to send 1947 whale-catch reports directly to the international statistics bureau.
subfiles.summary: Confirms the request will be passed to SCAP for direct reporting.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishing-area information for Hearst Newspapers
subfiles.about: Records the fishing-area boundaries given to a Hearst Newspapers representative.
subfiles.summary: Castleman corrected Karp’s belief that Japanese vessels could fish anywhere under international rules.

subfiles.title: Weekly Japanese Antarctic whale catch
subfiles.about: Reports whale catches for two Japanese factory ships during December 21–27.
subfiles.summary: Reports 32 blue-whale units for Hashidate Maru and 73 for Nisshin Maru.

subfiles.title: Status of U.S. policy for Japanese fishing
subfiles.about: Summarizes proposed fishing-area expansion and objections within the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Notes Chinese and Philippine objections, especially proximity to Luzon, and uncertainty over the meaning of “direct concern.”

subfiles.title: SCAP proposal to extend Japanese fishing area
subfiles.about: Proposes expanded fishing boundaries to increase Japanese food production and exports.
subfiles.summary: The partly garbled telegram outlines a larger fishing area and projects additional annual catch, export earnings, and reduced food-import costs. It requests comments on international, American industry, and Pacific command implications.

subfiles.title: File note on Tokyo whaling-observer despatch
subfiles.about: Comments on tensions among Allied observers aboard the Japanese whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Notes disputes with the Australian observer and Winston’s efforts to ensure Japanese compliance.

subfiles.title: Transmitting letter from SCAP Antarctic whaling observer
subfiles.about: Forwards Winston’s account of Australian and Norwegian observers aboard the whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Highlights radio disputes, catch logs, and excess observer rations.

subfiles.title: Winston’s letter concerning Allied whaling observers
subfiles.from: C. M. Adams, enclosing W. C. Winston’s letter
subfiles.about: Records Winston’s observations aboard Hashidate Maru during the 1947–48 Antarctic expedition.
subfiles.summary: Winston recounts conflict with Australian observer Coonan over direct radio messages and catch logs, while describing Norwegian observer Sundt as generally cooperative. He says Japanese crews changed whale-marking and numbering practices to comply with conventions. He also describes excessive rations, expired film, and daily life aboard ship.

subfiles.title: Official messages on whaling-expedition radio contacts
subfiles.from: W. C. Winston and SCAP Natural Resources Section
subfiles.to: SCAP Natural Resources Section and W. C. Winston
subfiles.about: Clarifies restrictions on direct radio contact from Japanese whaling ships.
subfiles.summary: SCAP allows specified contacts and states that the rules do not impose censorship.

subfiles.title: Duplicate despatch transmitting SCAP observer’s letter
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the despatch on Allied observers aboard the Japanese Antarctic expedition.
subfiles.summary: Again highlights the radio dispute, catch logs, and excess rations.

subfiles.title: Duplicate of Winston observer memorandum and letter
subfiles.from: C. M. Adams, enclosing W. C. Winston’s letter
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the memorandum and Winston letter reproduced on pages 99–104.
subfiles.summary: Repeats Winston’s account of disputes with Coonan, cooperation with Sundt, corrections to Japanese catch-recording practices, and problems with rations and film. The OCR is poorer than in the first copy.

subfiles.title: Duplicate radio messages on whaling-expedition communications
subfiles.from: W. C. Winston and SCAP Natural Resources Section
subfiles.to: SCAP Natural Resources Section and W. C. Winston
subfiles.about: Duplicate of the radio messages reproduced on page 105.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the rules for Japanese ship radio contacts and SCAP’s statement on censorship.

subfiles.title: Reply to J. E. Shields on Bering Sea fishing
subfiles.about: Refers Shields’s request about Japanese Bering Sea fishing to the Commerce Department.
subfiles.summary: Advises Shields that Commerce is responsible for the requested information.

subfiles.title: Reply to Representative Tollefson
subfiles.about: Refers a constituent’s Bering Sea fishing inquiry to the Commerce Department.
subfiles.summary: Says Commerce will handle the inquiry.

subfiles.title: Interdepartmental referral of Japanese fishing inquiry
subfiles.to: Chief, Far Eastern Branch, Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Transfers the inquiry about Japanese Bering Sea fishing for Commerce Department action.
subfiles.summary: Records a referral arranged by telephone with Commerce.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese cod-fishing records
subfiles.about: Requests the locations and results of Japanese cod fishing in the Bering Sea.
subfiles.summary: Shields recounts past competition with Japanese fishermen and asks where fish supplied to a San Francisco firm were caught.

subfiles.title: Tollefson forwards constituent’s fishing inquiry
subfiles.about: Requests action on a constituent’s question about Japanese Bering Sea fishing.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Shields’s letter and asks for information to relay to him.

subfiles.title: Proposals affecting Japanese fishing areas
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP Fisheries Division’s account of three proposed changes to Japanese fishing operations.
subfiles.summary: Identifies southern and northern area expansions and a possible 1948–49 Antarctic expedition.

subfiles.title: Fisheries Division excerpt on pending proposals
subfiles.from: SCAP Fisheries Division, Natural Resources Section
subfiles.about: Details pending fishing-area extensions and study of a third Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Notes Pacific command opposition to expansion into the Trust Territory and outlines a smaller northern boundary change.

subfiles.title: Conversation on imports of Japanese tuna
subfiles.about: Records concern from West Coast fishermen about rumored imports of frozen Japanese tuna.
subfiles.summary: Flory explains occupation export policy and requests a study of likely effects on the U.S. industry.

subfiles.title: Request for Formosan fisheries research material
subfiles.about: Seeks instructions on SCAP’s request for Japanese prewar fisheries research held in Taipei.
subfiles.summary: The requested material concerns spear fishes, tuna, sharks, and related biological data.

subfiles.title: Instruction on obtaining Formosan fisheries material
subfiles.about: Authorizes a discreet request for fisheries research material through the American consul in Taipei.
subfiles.summary: Says the consul may identify U.S. government interest without revealing SCAP’s role.

subfiles.title: Submission of policy paper on Japanese aquatic industries
subfiles.about: Submits a proposed U.S. policy paper on Japanese fishing and other aquatic industries.
subfiles.summary: Requests early subcommittee consideration of the enclosed policy paper.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of proposed SANACC paper
subfiles.about: Transmits the proposed Japanese fishing policy paper and its covering memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Routes the proposed SANACC paper for review.

subfiles.title: U.S. policy for Japanese fishing and other aquatic industries
subfiles.from: SANACC Subcommittee for the Far East
subfiles.about: Proposes U.S. policy for enlarging Japanese access to high-seas fisheries while observing conservation rules.
subfiles.summary: The paper argues for eventual Japanese access to high-seas fishing on terms comparable to other nations and strict observance of conservation agreements. It reviews occupation policy, the 1946 SCAP fishing boundary, proposed extensions, and Pacific command objections concerning the Trust Territory. Its proposed Far Eastern Commission text gives SCAP discretion to permit fishing within specified boundaries and to arrange access near areas under other countries’ jurisdiction.

subfiles.title: Proposed 1948–49 whaling expedition: Australia
subfiles.about: Invites Australian views on a proposed third SCAP-administered Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Describes plans for three factory ships, Allied observers, compliance with whaling rules, and international allocation of whale oil.

subfiles.title: Proposed 1948–49 whaling expedition: Norway
subfiles.about: Invites Norwegian views on a proposed third SCAP-administered Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Describes plans for three factory ships, Allied observers, compliance with whaling rules, and international allocation of whale oil.

subfiles.title: Proposed 1948–49 whaling expedition: Britain
subfiles.about: Invites British views under an earlier undertaking to consult on a further Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Reports the proposed expedition, expected use of three factory ships, observer access, and compliance and whale-oil allocation assurances.

subfiles.title: Proposed 1948–49 whaling expedition: New Zealand
subfiles.about: Invites New Zealand views on a proposed third SCAP-administered Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Describes plans for three factory ships, Allied observers, compliance with whaling rules, and international allocation of whale oil.

subfiles.title: Australian concerns over unilateral occupation decisions
subfiles.about: Objects to occupation decisions made without Far Eastern Commission consideration, including another Japanese whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: Lists Japanese whaling, a SCAP press release, and Japanese coastal patrol as examples of unilateral action.
